The suggested design is demonstrated through the synthesis of an LPV <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>robust vehicle sideslip angle observer. Furthermore, a dSPACE-ASM simulation study is conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness and the advantage of the proposed polytopic construction over a baseline approach.

articleTitle: How Uncertainty Affects Test Results for Driving Automation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Automated Vehicle Validation Conference (IAVVC)
abstract: Given the increasing test efforts required for Advanced Driver Assistance Systems and higher driving automation, a variety of test environments has to be leveraged. Ranging from virtual X-in-the-Loop to real-world testing, each test environment entails uncertainties which can be aleatory and/or epistemic. We introduce different sources of uncertainties and discuss their type and allocation to respective test environments. While X-in-the-Loop environments are mainly prone to epistemic uncertainty due to the simplification of simulation models, a substantial part of the uncertainty of real-world testing is aleatory due to nondeterministic effects from driver and environment. Given a nondeterministic test environment, we introduce a method to estimate confidence intervals for test result probabilities based on a multinomial distribution. This method is applied to a scenario for an Advanced Emergency Braking System. It can be shown that based on the confidence intervals, the system meets a predefined minimum performance and test results have sufficient statistical significance. Applying the method to a reduced test set indicates that a lower number of executions can undermine both the argumentation for minimum performance and test result significance.

articleTitle: RotICP: A Spherical-Based Distance Algorithm for Rotation Search and Point Cloud Registration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Automated Vehicle Validation Conference (IAVVC)
abstract: The Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm is one of the most widely used point cloud registration methods with a well known problem of requiring a good initial guess to reach a satisfactory solution. In particular, the ICP may encounter issues with large initial differences between point clouds, especially regarding the rotation. We contribute a new iterative algorithm, named RotICP, which solves the challenging simultaneous rotation and correspondence search registration problem in a vastly more robust way than compared methods. The RotICP handles rotations in a natural manner using a proposed spherical-based distance measure which captures an intuitive notion of ‘rotational closeness’. We additionally prove a theorem that RotICP converges monotonically to a local minima and compare it with the classical ICP and one state-of-the-art registration algorithm on numerous simultaneous rotation and correspondence search registration problems including both synthetic and real-world data. The results show that RotICP not only handles large rotations significantly better than the other methods, but also converges in significantly less iterations than ICP while achieving state-of-the-art accuracy.

articleTitle: Structured Testing Framework for ADAS Algorithm Development
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Automated Vehicle Validation Conference (IAVVC)
abstract: Formalized software testing is becoming increasingly common for software teams. However, existing frameworks suffer from test development that is inflexible and tedious to update as the software stack itself changes. Additionally, the time and resources spent in creating test cases can often be a deterrent for continual test case development. This paper proposes a testing framework, called structured testing, that works at both integration and system test levels in ROS 2. Though primarily built for ADAS/AV development, it is flexible to adaption for other domains. It focuses on intuitive test specification and a simulator agnostic input in the form of ROS bag files. Additionally, though integrated with Gitlab's CI tool as an example, it is integrable with any similar standard CI tool for test automation. The framework is compared to the standard ROS 2 integration testing protocol and shows comparative improvements in ease of use as well as a reduction in compute resource consumption.

articleTitle: Multi-User Real-Time Controllable Connected Cars Testing Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Automated Vehicle Validation Conference (IAVVC)
abstract: V2X communication improves safety and information sharing among vehicles and other stakeholders in traffic. The information shared between connected cars enables the development of numerous applications. Application of technologies to the real world is not possible without comprehensive testing. Many testing methodologies exist to verify and validate developed technologies. Each of these methodologies has trade-offs in terms of realism, cost, repeatability, reliability, and time criteria. With the aim of optimizing this trade-off, we have developed a human-in-the-loop test platform where application tests of connected cars can be conducted. This platform enables multiple users to drive their own virtual vehicles through keyboard and test V2X applications. To demonstrate the performance of our test platform, internal delay measurements were conducted. The measurements revealed negligible delays. Additionally, to showcase the feasibility of application testing on our platform, a simple LCRW application was implemented. The application test demonstrated that the developed algorithm responded as expected, providing the necessary warnings to the user regarding collision risks.
